title: τ 2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
abstract: τ 2-Bench is a novel benchmark for conversational AI agents that evaluates their ability to coordinate with a user in a dual-control environment. The benchmark introduces a telecom domain where both the agent and user have distinct tools to observe, act upon, and verify the state of a shared, dynamic environment.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're a customer support agent trying to help a user troubleshoot their mobile data issue. You need to guide the user to take specific actions, like checking their status bar or toggling their data, while also using your own tools to resolve the issue. This is a dual-control environment, where both you and the user have agency.

τ 2-Bench is designed to test conversational AI agents in such scenarios, where they must coordinate with a user to solve a task.

steps.label: Agent Asks User to Check Status Bar

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
τ 2-Bench uses a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) to model the dual-control environment. The agent and user interact with each other and their respective tools, receiving observations and rewards based on their actions.

The benchmark includes a telecom domain with 5 plans, 9 lines, and 4 customers, and 114 tasks that test the agent's ability to coordinate with the user.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
The benchmark results show that state-of-the-art language models struggle to coordinate with the user in the dual-control environment. The pass^k metric, which measures the fraction of tasks that are successfully completed, is significantly lower than in single-control environments.

For example, the gpt-4.1 model achieves a pass^1 of 34% in the telecom domain, while the o4-mini model achieves a pass^1 of 42%.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The results of τ 2-Bench highlight the challenges of guiding users in a dual-control environment. The benchmark shows that current language models struggle to coordinate with users, even in simple tasks.

This has significant implications for the development of conversational AI agents, as it highlights the need for more advanced models that can effectively guide users and coordinate with them to solve tasks.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
τ 2-Bench introduces several key innovations, including a novel dual-control telecom domain, a compositional task generator, and a reliable user simulator.

The benchmark also enables fine-grained analysis of agent performance, allowing developers to identify areas for improvement and develop more effective conversational AI agents.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
τ 2-Bench is an open-source benchmark, and developers can try it out themselves to evaluate the performance of their conversational AI agents.

The benchmark includes a range of tools and resources, including a user simulator, a task generator, and a evaluation metric, to help developers improve their agents and develop more effective conversational AI systems.
